questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{3\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{3\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{7\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{-1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={270}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{270}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{270}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{270}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-1) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
